question: In ∆ABC, the perpendiculars drawn from A, B and C meet the opposite sides at points D, E and F, respectively. AD, BE and CF intersect at point P. If ∠EPD = 110° and the bisectors of ∠A and ∠B meet at point Q, then ∠AQB = ?
solution:
**Given:**

∠EPD = 110°

**Concept used:**

In ΔABC if angle bisector of ∠B and ∠C meet at a point O inside the triangle then

∠BOC = 90° + ∠A/2

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9ef00ae35366d15a977df4c6c9da30337774e2da6190b658219a2727f956bb5b.png] 

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/bd28067a01cf7d1bd572af8e4593152762bf8685623fd5d738708b3727a9336b.png] 

In the diagram

DPEC is quadrilateral

Now,

∠C = 360° - (∠P + ∠D + ∠E)

⇒ ∠C = 360° - (110° + 90° + 90°)

⇒ ∠C = 360° - 290°

⇒ ∠C = 70°

According to the concept,

∠AQB = 90° + 70/2

⇒ ∠AQB = 90° + 35°

⇒ ∠AQB = 125°

**∴ ∠AQB is 125°.**
